correctness.rationale: All defining hypotheses and boundaries are explicit. The incidence-row expansion bounds EVERY determinant of both relation matrix and every label-difference augmented matrix by 2^k. When p>2^k, this controls p-saturation and permits the exact p^-2 collision probability in both groups. The strict union bound follows from t<=3k and binom(3k,2)<4^k. The addition-chain witness is valid in C_{p^2} and impossible in exponent-p groups, proving both bounds. Exact examples and Fermat/Mersenne cases are checked against chain lengths; the finite checker is corroborative only.

value.rationale: It proves a uniform logarithmic information lower bound for arbitrary sparse multiplication patterns in prime-square groups; establishes entire Mersenne- and Fermat-prime exact families plus several other exact cases; and solves a sharp three-entry threshold and the natural first unlisted orders 25,49,121. The proof identifies a structural bridge from sparse group tables to totally unimodular incidence matrices and probabilistic separating maps, not a routine data point.
